Summary  
The source is a short opinion piece arguing that a public “adversarial collaboration” between an AI-safety researcher who believes in existential-risk (x-risk) from AI and a respected AI expert who is sceptical would improve the quality of the debate and, consequently, downstream policy and safety decisions. It discusses the benefits, possible failure modes, and feasibility of such a collaboration, citing Daniel Kahneman’s original conception and a few related precedents.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[78]  
The fabric contains every explicit causal claim linking the polarised x-risk debate (risk) through its analysed causes, the theoretical promise of adversarial collaboration, design rationales for making it public, concrete implementation mechanisms, limited historical validation evidence, and the single actionable intervention proposed. Instructions could be improved by including explicit examples for social-process interventions (not just model-centric ones) to clarify lifecycle tagging for policy/epistemic actions.

Inference strategy justification  
The text is largely conceptual; therefore light inference (edge confidence = 2) was used to:  
1. Formulate the systemic risk (“inadequate AI safety policymaking”) implied but not verbatim.  
2. Distil two complementary implementation mechanisms from narrative descriptions.  
No moderate inference (confidence = 1) was required.

Extraction completeness explanation  
Every distinct claim affecting the core reasoning chain was captured (11 nodes, ~15 nodes per 5 000 w guideline ⇒ appropriate). All nodes are connected in a single fabric; no satellites remain.

Key limitations  
• Validation evidence is anecdotal; edge confidences are therefore low-medium.  
• The intervention lifecycle taxonomy is model-centric; “6-Other” was the closest fit for a discourse intervention.  
• The text is brief, so the fabric is correspondingly small.
